changelog.summary: Says where CodeBoarding gets its AI credentials, and fails with the missing secret named instead of quietly running on a different provider.
changelog.detail: First template tracked by version. Everything committed before this is recognised by content, and described by this entry.

templates.review:
name: CodeBoarding review

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, reopened, ready_for_review, closed, synchronize]
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]

# No workflow-level permissions: each job requests only what it needs (least
# privilege), so the default token starts with none.
permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: codeboarding-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action == 'closed' }}

jobs:
  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read        # check out the repo + read the committed baseline (no writes in review mode)
      pull-requests: write  # post the architecture-diff PR comment
      issues: write         # the /codeboarding issue_comment trigger + comment API
{{OIDC_PERMISSION}}      actions: read         # let a repeat review download the analysis an earlier run published, instead of re-deriving the whole PR
    if: >
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action != 'closed' &&
       github.event.pull_request.draft == false &&
       github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository{{SYNC_PR_GUARD}}) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && github.event.issue.pull_request != null &&
       startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/codeboarding') &&
       contains(fromJSON('["OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR"]'), github.event.comment.author_association))
    steps:
      - uses: CodeBoarding/CodeBoarding-action@v1
        with:
{{CREDENTIALS}}
templates.sync:
name: CodeBoarding sync

on:
  push:
    branches: ['{{BRANCH}}']
    # Loop guard: don't re-trigger on the files this workflow itself commits.
    # List generated files only: user-authored scope configuration must still trigger
    # regeneration, while a merged sync PR must not trigger a loop.
    paths-ignore:
      - '.codeboarding/*.md'
      - '.codeboarding/analysis.json'
      - '.codeboarding/fingerprint.json'
      - '.codeboarding/static_analysis.pkl'
      - '.codeboarding/static_analysis.sha'
      - '.codeboarding/codeboarding_version.json'
      - '.codeboarding/health/health_report.json'
      - 'docs/development/architecture.md'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      force_full:
        description: 'Ignore the committed baseline and rebuild it from scratch (full analysis).'
        type: boolean
        required: false
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: write   # commit the generated baseline + docs to the branch
{{EXTRA_PERMISSIONS}}
concurrency:
  # Serialize against itself so a push landing mid-run can't make two commits.
  group: codeboarding-sync
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: CodeBoarding/CodeBoarding-action@v1
        with:
          mode: sync
          force_full: ${{ inputs.force_full || false }}
{{DELIVERY_INPUT}}          target_branch: '{{BRANCH}}'
{{CREDENTIALS}}

credentials.hosted:
# CodeBoarding's free hosted tier. No secret to add: the run authenticates
          # with the GitHub OIDC token that `id-token: write` above grants.
          llm: hosted
credentials.license:
# Your CodeBoarding plan, on CodeBoarding's hosted tier. The run fails with
          # a message naming this secret if CODEBOARDING_LICENSE is not set.
          llm: license
          license_key: ${{ secrets.CODEBOARDING_LICENSE }}
credentials.byok:openrouter:
# Your own OpenRouter key: every run calls OpenRouter directly with it.
          # Add OPENROUTER_API_KEY under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Until it
          # exists the run FAILS and says so. It does not fall back to a different
          # provider on CodeBoarding's hosted tier.
          llm: openrouter
          openrouter_api_key: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
credentials.byok:orcarouter:
# Your own OrcaRouter key: every run calls OrcaRouter directly with it.
          # Add ORCAROUTER_API_KEY under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Until it
          # exists the run FAILS and says so. It does not fall back to a different
          # provider on CodeBoarding's hosted tier.
          llm: orcarouter
          orcarouter_api_key: ${{ secrets.ORCAROUTER_API_KEY }}
credentials.byok:anthropic:
# Your own Anthropic key: every run calls Anthropic directly with it.
          # Add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Until it
          # exists the run FAILS and says so. It does not fall back to a different
          # provider on CodeBoarding's hosted tier.
          llm: anthropic
          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
credentials.byok:openai:
# Your own OpenAI key: every run calls OpenAI directly with it.
          # Add OPENAI_API_KEY under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Until it
          # exists the run FAILS and says so. It does not fall back to a different
          # provider on CodeBoarding's hosted tier.
          llm: openai
          openai_api_key: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
credentials.byok:google:
# Your own Google Gemini key: every run calls Google Gemini directly with it.
          # Add GOOGLE_API_KEY under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Until it
          # exists the run FAILS and says so. It does not fall back to a different
          # provider on CodeBoarding's hosted tier.
          llm: google
          google_api_key: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
credentials.byok:vercel:
# Your own Vercel AI Gateway key: every run calls Vercel AI Gateway directly with it.
          # Add VERCEL_API_KEY under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Until it
          # exists the run FAILS and says so. It does not fall back to a different
          # provider on CodeBoarding's hosted tier.
          llm: vercel
          vercel_api_key: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_API_KEY }}
credentials.byok:aws_bedrock:
# Your own AWS Bedrock key: every run calls AWS Bedrock directly with it.
          # Add AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Until it
          # exists the run FAILS and says so. It does not fall back to a different
          # provider on CodeBoarding's hosted tier.
          llm: aws_bedrock
          aws_bedrock_api_key: ${{ secrets.AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK }}
credentials.byok:cerebras:
# Your own Cerebras key: every run calls Cerebras directly with it.
          # Add CEREBRAS_API_KEY under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Until it
          # exists the run FAILS and says so. It does not fall back to a different
          # provider on CodeBoarding's hosted tier.
          llm: cerebras
          cerebras_api_key: ${{ secrets.CEREBRAS_API_KEY }}
credentials.byok:deepseek:
# Your own DeepSeek key: every run calls DeepSeek directly with it.
          # Add DEEPSEEK_API_KEY under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Until it
          # exists the run FAILS and says so. It does not fall back to a different
          # provider on CodeBoarding's hosted tier.
          llm: deepseek
          deepseek_api_key: ${{ secrets.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY }}
credentials.byok:glm:
# Your own GLM key: every run calls GLM directly with it.
          # Add GLM_API_KEY under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Until it
          # exists the run FAILS and says so. It does not fall back to a different
          # provider on CodeBoarding's hosted tier.
          llm: glm
          glm_api_key: ${{ secrets.GLM_API_KEY }}
credentials.byok:kimi:
# Your own Kimi key: every run calls Kimi directly with it.
          # Add KIMI_API_KEY under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Until it
          # exists the run FAILS and says so. It does not fall back to a different
          # provider on CodeBoarding's hosted tier.
          llm: kimi
          kimi_api_key: ${{ secrets.KIMI_API_KEY }}
credentials.byok:ollama:
# Your own Ollama endpoint: every run calls it directly.
          # ollama is selected by its endpoint rather than a key, so set
          # ollama_base_url to the address CodeBoarding should reach it on. Until it
          # is set the run FAILS and says so. It does not fall back to a different
          # provider on CodeBoarding's hosted tier.
          llm: ollama
          ollama_base_url: https://your-ollama-host
credentials.byok:litellm:
# Your own LiteLLM endpoint: every run calls it directly.
          # litellm is selected by its endpoint rather than a key, so set
          # litellm_base_url to the address CodeBoarding should reach it on. Until it
          # is set the run FAILS and says so. It does not fall back to a different
          # provider on CodeBoarding's hosted tier.
          llm: litellm
          litellm_base_url: https://your-litellm-host

review.hosted: id-token: write       # mint a GitHub OIDC token for CodeBoarding's hosted tier

sync.hosted:
id-token: write   # identifies this repo to CodeBoarding's hosted tier; a run on your own
                    # provider key never mints one, so it is not granted there

pull_request.permission: pull-requests: write # open/update the rolling baseline PR for a protected target branch
